problems.explain: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180°: each is half the arc it stands on, and the two arcs make the whole 360°. ∠D is opposite ∠B, so ∠D = 180 − 100 = 80°. (∠A is beside it, not opposite: neighboring corners need not add to 180°.) So ∠D = 80°.

problems.explain: ∠ACB and ∠ADB both stand on arc AB from the same side, and each is half of it. So ∠ADB = 74 ÷ 2 = 37°, and so is the other angle on that arc. (Not 74°: that would be the central angle.) So ∠ADB = 37°.
